question: Related Questions Q. i am a goverment servent having limited source of income i hardly manage to save some amount of money for the welfare of my children as the inflation goes up what is the islamic way to invest my money so that i can get at the end of retirement handsome amount for the welfare of the family. 1817 views Q. Is it permissible for one to get a lawyer after he is injured in an accident, and then go to court, and get a dollar value that is beyond the damage done to him/her. 1540 views Q. Salaamolaikum, I reside in a rented house and end up paying significant money as rent, I do not have an own house. In this context am I allowed to avail a loan from a bank and buy or construct a house and then pay back the money in instalments, knowing that the bank is going to add interest to the principle when getting back the loan? Also this loan will help me in getting significant rebate on my taxable money(income tax). 1728 views Q. I'm from India but currently residing in Sharjah, U.A.E. in a rented accommodation. Before going to India for a vacation of two months, my neighbours requested our flat for the stay of their guests during our absence. They said that their guests shall pay the rent to me for their stay & settle other bills like electricity, etc. I took some advance amount before going to India and handed-over the possesion of my flat to their guests. After coming back from vacation & taking back the possession of my flat, I got a doubt whether I had done the right act. I checked my tenancy contract and found a condition that says "Tenant has no right to waive or sublease property for investment, unless authorized by the Department of Economic Development in the emirate and with a written approval of the lessor (i.e. owner)". Kindly let me know whether I have violated the above condition. I would like to know the following: a) Whether the amount received from my neighbours' guests would be halal? b) If not halal, what should I do with the money? should I give it in Charity or should I give it back to the concerned person after dedcuting the repair charges, etc.? c) If I could not find the person from whom I received the rent amount or if the person refuses to take back the amount, what should I do? Anticipating your reply as soon as possible. 1910 views Q. I want to ask is network marketing is allowed in islam? answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Other Transactions Question ID: 7501 Country: India Title: Hazrat my doubt is one of my cousin given me some huge amount of money and said spend as u like and at that time i have some depts so i accepted the money,he didnt said any thing about returning the money to him.Do i have to pay him back the money he has given.the problem is, due to some family fight we are not in talks and my parents feel some harm from them, my parents has given me a strict warning not to speak to him or his family.Can you please guide, if i talk to him i'll disobey my parents.how can i know that it was not a loan or he just help me. Allah Hafiz(Jazakallahu-Khairan) Question: Assalam u Alaikum. Hazrat my doubt is one of my cousin given me some huge amount of money and said spend as u like and at that time i have some depts so i accepted the money,he didnt said any thing about returning the money to him.Do i have to pay him back the money he has given.the problem is, due to some family fight we are not in talks and my parents feel some harm from them, my parents has given me a strict warning not to speak to him or his family.Can you please guide, if i talk to him i'll disobey my parents.how can i know that it was not a loan or he just help me. Allah Hafiz(Jazakallahu-Khairan) Answer ID: 7501 Posted on: Aug 29, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1160/1003=L/1429) If your cousin, while giving you the money, did neither specify it as debt nor there is any indication of the same, then it will be considered as gift and you do not have to return it back. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
